subject: Post-demo: bursting, multi-region latency & data sovereignty — next steps
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Liu <anna@nubisoft.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + performance asks (bursting & residency)

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning — great discussion. Below is a concise recap of the performance and residency items we discussed and the immediate asks so we can size a short pilot.

TL;DR: We heard: P95 latency targets, streaming interactivity, sustained throughput + short spikes, and strict EU data residency for EU tenants. Action items at the bottom.

Key constraints / targets we captured from the call:
- Target P95 (generation only, server-side) for typical short-completions: <= 120 ms in US regions (goal).
- Streaming/interactive: token-by-token latency must feel < 200 ms end-to-end for EU and US users (APAC target slightly higher ~250ms).
- Baseline throughput: ~40k tokens/sec across the account during business hours; baseline concurrency ~200 concurrent streams.
- Expected bursts: up to 1.2k concurrent users for 60–120 minute morning spike windows (can happen in multiple timezones).
- Cold vs warm: some flows reuse large prefixes (KV cache will help); others are new per request.
- Data residency: EU customer data and logs must remain in EU regions with 90 day retention; APAC customers must not cross EU/US for raw request payloads.

Questions / clarifications we need from you to size pilot and recommend infra:
1) Can you share a small sample traffic profile (CSV or histogram) showing requests/s by minute for a typical day and a spike day?
2) For the streaming use-case: is the UI expecting token streaming from the server to the client (chunked responses) or are you planning server-side assembly + single response?
3) Which pieces of telemetry/PII must remain in-region vs what can be aggregated (e.g., metrics/latency logs)?

What we propose next:
- We’ll provision a short pilot that can: 1) validate P95 under your spike shape, 2) test streaming latency from EU and APAC, and 3) confirm residency for request logs.
- Attach: redwood_slo_template.xlsx — a short SLO matrix we’ll populate and return with initial recommendations (shard/residency, burst pool sizing, estimated token-cost).
- Next call: Technical deep-dive w/ Ben (solutions engineer) and Marissa (CS/ops) — available Wed/Thu this week.

Please reply with the sample traffic and confirm whether streaming is token-level or assembled. I’ll get Ben to run a bench against a simulated profile once we have the traffic shape.

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + performance asks (bursting & residency)

Thanks, Rafael — this aligns with our notes. Quick answers and clarifications below.

- Streaming: we need token-level streaming (client expects incremental tokens; assembly on client). Typical UI target is <200 ms perceived token latency for EU/US.
- The 120 ms p95: that is intended as total server-side generation time (we understand network will add some RTT; include that in your estimates).
- Traffic profile: attached is a small sample payload and a CSV with per-minute counts for a typical weekday and for the largest spike day last quarter. Morning spikes occur ~09:00–11:30 local time, often hitting ~1.2k concurrent for 45–90 minutes.
- Residency: EU tenant requests and raw logs must remain in EU. Aggregated performance metrics can be replicated to US for dashboarding but raw request payloads and trace logs must not leave EU. Retention requirement: 90 days for raw logs.
- Pilot: procurement is ~6 weeks to sign, but we can start a technical pilot earlier if terms are acceptable.

Two asks for you:
1) Can you confirm whether the 120 ms p95 is measured before network egress to client or after?
2) If we need 2x redundancy in APAC, what would that do to the burst capacity/cost estimates?

Sample files attached: sample_payload.json, traffic_histogram_weekday.csv

— Anna

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + performance asks (bursting & residency)

Anna — great, thanks for the fast follow-up and for the attachments. Looping Ben for benching and Marissa for pilot coordination and compliance questions.

Quick clarifications from our side (short answers):
- The 120 ms p95 I listed was intended as server-side generation only (compute time). Network egress to the client will add additional RTT; typical additional latency is ~20–60 ms depending on region and CDN path. For strict perceived latency we should target ~80–100 ms server-side p95 to hit ~200 ms end-to-end in many cases.
- Streaming: we support chunked token streaming over HTTP/2 and websockets. For interactive flows we typically see per-token arrival windows of 40–100 ms when the model is warmed; cold starts and long prefixes can increase that. KV caching can reduce compute on prefix-heavy sessions.
- Bursting: for the spike shapes you shared, we recommend a dedicated pool (reserved) with a burst buffer (hot spare instances + autoscale headroom). If you want 2x APAC redundancy, plan for ~1.7–1.9x the baseline burst capacity (not a straight 2x due to shared cold/warm effects). We’ll map cost vs SLO risk in the SLO matrix.

Planned next steps (owners & rough ETA):
- Ben: run bench with your sample_payload + histogram shape — aim to publish a bench report Tue COB (ETA: 2027-08-03).
- Rafael: fill and return the SLO matrix with recommended pool sizing and cost delta (ETA: Wed).
- Marissa: confirm compliance constraints and scope of in-region log retention (ETA: Wed).

Scheduling: here’s a short availability poll for the technical deep-dive: https://cal.com/redwood/tech-deep-dive (please pick a 45m slot).

I’ll attach a preliminary SLO matrix back after Ben’s bench.

Best — Rafael

Thanks — I started the bench this morning against a small cluster that mimics your shape. Early notes:
- With a warmed model and KV cache, server-side p95 for short completions is ~85–110 ms in US-west at the settings I used (I’ll share numbers for EU/APAC after the run completes).
- Token streaming per-chunk latency is ~45–90 ms when using our streaming hooks; spikes push that up predictably.
- Under a synthetic 1.2k concurrent morning spike I saw increased tail due to concurrency limits on a single shard; we can mitigate with multi-shard routing and a burst pool.

Planned deliverables:
1) Full bench report with tables by region and traffic shape (shared Wed morning).
2) SLO matrix with recommended pool sizes and expected cost buckets (I’ll contribute the numbers — Rafael will assemble the doc).
3) Pilot configuration draft (Marissa to finalize compliance checklist).

I’ll attach a tiny placeholder bench-results-placeholder.txt and will follow up with the detailed CSVs.

Ben
